title: Engagement Vitals — operator notes and KPI primer
body:
Purpose:
This is a short operator-facing primer for the QBR-style KPI table we surface to customer teams. Focus: canonical definitions (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate), short queries or heuristics engineers can use during an account review, and a compact KPI table with suggested targets and alerting thresholds.

Audience:
- Customer Success (owners and managers)
- Solutions & SRE on-call when we dig into renewal signals
- Product managers prepping QBR slides

Notes-to-self style (informal):
- Keep examples SQL-ish but vendor-neutral (logs have timestamps, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, route, cache_status).
- Provide quick remediation checklist for each metric.
- This doc is intentionally terse – meant to be copy-paste into review decks.

Metric definitions (short):
1) Latency (production generation latency)
   - Definition: wall-clock time between request received and final token delivered (stream end) measured in milliseconds.
   - Common quantiles: p50, p90, p99. Use p90 for QBR narratives, p99 for SRE escalations.
   - Basic computation (pseudo-SQL):
       SELECT
         percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p50,
         percentile_cont(0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p90,
         percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99
       FROM request_logs
       WHERE date BETWEEN '{{start}}' AND '{{end}}' AND route = '{{customer_route}}';
   - Units: ms. Typical customer target buckets we show in QBR: p90 <= 250ms (interactive features), p90 <= 800ms (background async).
   - Why it matters: user-perceived interactivity & error surface for timeouts. Also drives cost via longer open connections for streaming.
   - Quick remediation checklist (if p90 increases):
       * Check model variant and version rollout (did we route to a larger model?).
       * Inspect batch sizes and queue length in serving logs.
       * Look for region routing / cross-region hops.
       * Check cache hit rate (low cache -> more cold generation).
       * If p99 spikes, look for specific request shapes (very long context, huge output).

2) Uptime (service availability)
   - Definition: percentage of successful requests (2xx) over total requests in a window, excluding planned maintenance. For more strict SLOs use route-level health probes.
   - Formula (simple): uptime_pct = 100 * (successful_requests / total_requests) over rolling 30d or N-day window.
   - QBR-friendly SLOs: 99.9% monthly for Dedicated customers; 99.5% for small-hosted tiers.
   - Example alerting: paging when hourly error rate > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
   - Quick remediate: check recent deploys, autoscale failures, GPU OOMs, fallback path (did fallback model succeed?).

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
   - Definition: total inference spend / total billed tokens (or tokens_in + tokens_out depending on billing).
   - Example calc: if month spend = $12,000 and tokens billed = 120M => cost/token = $0.0001 per token.
   - Why it matters: ties directly to renewal conversations and efficiency suggestions (quantize models, cache warm prefixes, shorten prompts).
   - Quick analysis query (pseudo):
       SELECT sum(cost_usd) / nullif(sum(billed_tokens),0) as cost_per_token
       FROM billing_events
       WHERE customer_id = '{{cid}}' AND month = '{{YYYY-MM}}';
   - Notes: watch for sudden token inflation (change in average prompt length or increase in sampling temperature causing longer outputs).

4) Cache hit rate (request-level prefix cache)
   - Definition: fraction of requests served from cache (exact or prefix KV) vs total eligible requests. cache_hit_rate = cache_hits / cache_eligible_requests.
   - When to compute: only include requests where caching is enabled and requests match cache eligibility rules.
   - Example: month cache hits = 2,400,000, eligible = 6,000,000 => cache_hit_rate = 40%.
   - Why it matters: cache reduces tokens generated, lowers cost/token and latency for repeat prompts.
   - Quick checks when cache hit rate low: inconsistent prompt prefixing (dynamic IDs in prompt), TTL too short, policy mismatch (route-level fallback to non-cacheable variant).

Compact KPI table (copyable plain-text for QBR slide)
Columns: metric | canonical_measure | window | target | escalation_threshold | owner | how-we-measure | quick-action
Rows (examples):
- Latency (p90) | p90 latency_ms | 30d | <=250ms (interactive) | >500ms for 1h | eng-sre | p90 over request_logs filtered by route | check batching/model/region/caching
- Uptime | successful_requests/total_requests (%) | 30d | >=99.9% (dedicated) | <99% for 24h | eng-sre | rolling error rate from infra metrics | rollback / failover / investigate autoscaler
- Cost per token | spend_usd / billed_tokens | 30d | <= $0.00012 | >2x trend over 7d | customer-success | billing_events join usage | inspect token counts & prompts, recommend quantize/cache
- Cache hit rate | cache_hits / eligible_requests (%) | 30d | >=45% (where cache applicable) | <20% for 7d | solutions-eng | cache logs or cache_metrics | validate prompt templates, raise TTL or template changes

Example KPI table row as CSV (for quick copy):
metric,measure,window,target,threshold,owner,query_hint
latency_p90,p90_latency_ms,30d,"<=250"," >500 1h",eng-sre,"percentile_cont(0.90) FROM request_logs WHERE route=..."

Example calculations (realistic numbers):
- Week sample: total_requests = 350k, successful = 349k => uptime = 99.71% (ok for hosted, review for Dedicated).
- Latency: p50=120ms, p90=280ms, p99=940ms -> narrative: tail latency issue; highlight p90 miss vs goal.
- Cost: spend = $6,240, billed_tokens = 52M -> cost/token = $0.00012. If tokens/month double next month cost doubles (unless cache/batching change).
- Cache: eligible=1.2M, hits=540k -> hit_rate=45% -> roughly halves token-volume for cached traffic.

Operator playbooks (very short):
- Latency elevated (p90 > target):
   1) Check recent deployments: did we flip traffic to a larger model? (link PRs)
   2) Inspect serving queue/backpressure metrics and batching latency. If queue depth high, consider temporary burst capacity.
   3) Check cache hit rate — cold cache can raise p90. If cache low, ask product for templating fixes.
   4) If region-specific, try routing to alternative region with similar SLA.

- Cost spike:
   1) Query top routes by spend (last 24h).
   2) Look at average tokens per request and distribution (are a few requests creating very long outputs?).
   3) Recommend immediate mitigations: enable tighter output token limits, lower sampling temperature, enable higher cache TTLs.

- Cache hit drop:
   1) Sample prompt texts (anonymized) to see template drift (IDs or timestamps injected).
   2) Check cache eligibility config and recent code changes to prompt construction.

Quick diagnostics (copyable snippets):
- Top 10 routes by token spend (pseudo-SQL):
    SELECT route, sum(billed_tokens) as tokens, sum(cost_usd) as spend
    FROM billing_events
    WHERE customer_id = '{{cid}}' AND date >= '{{start}}'
    GROUP BY route
    ORDER BY tokens desc
    LIMIT 10;

- Cache hit time series (last 30d):
    Plot daily cache_hits / cache_eligible as percentage. Look for step changes aligning to deploys.

Unresolved questions / followups (to capture before QBR):
- Decide canonical billing token definition for Table (some products include only output tokens). Put a hard note in QBR slide.
- Agree on route-level targets for mid-market customers (we use hosted defaults now).
- Ask solutions-eng for sample prompt templates to compute "cache-eligibility" for large accounts.

Next steps (owner & timeline):
- Priya: make a single-slide export for the next QBR deck (due 2025-02-10).
- Ethan: add example alert runbook links to ops playbook (due 2025-02-01).
- Marta: audit top 10 customer routes for cache policy drift and share list (due 2025-02-07).

Footer (informal):
- This doc is a working cheat sheet. Keep it blunt and usable in calls. If we need a more formal handbook, migrate to Confluence and link back to this draft.
- Notes: leave raw SQL examples as pseudocode; production tables differ across orgs.
